title: Constant-module realization identifies derived tensors, adjunctions and projection maps
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be sites small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], $A$ a finite discrete commutative ring, and $w:\operatorname{Sh}(D,K)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C,J)$ a geometric morphism. Give it the constant-section-preserving ring isomorphism $c:w^{-1}\underline A_C\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline A_D$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $E_C:\operatorname{Sh}(C,J;\operatorname{Mod}_A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_C)$ and $E_D$ be the constant-scalar equivalences, normalized to preserve the underlying additive sheaf and constant scalar actions [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-constant-ring-equivalence]. On the fixed-$A$ side use the sheafified tensor over $A$, its direct-sum K-flat derived tensor, the exact module inverse image $w_A^*$ and the canonical derived adjunction $w_A^*\dashv Rw_{*,A}$ obtained from the ordinary constant-scalar comparison [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-geometric-adjunctions]; on the ringed side use extension of scalars along $c$, canonical K-flat derived pullback, derived tensor and the K-injective derived adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. All derived categories are ordinary and uncompleted [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Flatness and K-flatness mean exactness of tensor and preservation of acyclic complexes by total tensor, respectively [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. The equivalences $E_C,E_D$ are the constant-scalar restrictions with their tensor comparisons, flat/K-flat preservation and signed total-tensor identifications of [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor]. The fixed-$A$ pullback tensor comparison $w_A^*(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)\to w_A^*M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}w_A^*N$ is the one computed on flat-term K-flat representatives by the map $w_A^*(P\otimes_AQ)\to w_A^*P\otimes_Aw_A^*Q$ sending each local pure tensor to the corresponding pure tensor.
The induced equivalences $D(E_C),D(E_D)$ identify these derived tensors and pullback/direct-image functors, including their specified adjunction Hom bijections, units and counits. Under these identifications the fixed-$A$ pullback tensor comparison is exactly the ringed comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], for every pair of unbounded inputs. Consequently the fixed-$A$ projection map defined as the adjunct of counit tensor identity after this comparison is the specified ringed projection map, naturally in both inputs. These identifications also commute with the canonical inclusions $D^+\hookrightarrow D$ and the bounded-below/unbounded direct-image comparisons; the included bounded-below counit is the unbounded counit at the included object. Here $D^+$ is the full subcategory of complexes with cohomology zero in all sufficiently negative degrees. In particular, when $(C,J),(D,K)$ are the small etale sites of schemes $Y,X$ and $w=f_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a morphism $f:X\to Y$, the module inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (the inverse image of the underlying abelian sheaf with transported action, with the abelian unit and counit) corresponds under $E_C,E_D$ to $w_A^*$ with its adjunction, the comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] corresponds to the inverse of the fixed-$A$ pullback tensor comparison, and the projection-formula morphism $\mathrm{PF}_f$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] (with $\Lambda=A$) corresponds to the fixed-$A$ projection map; hence $\mathrm{PF}_f$ is the specified ringed projection map of $f_{\mathrm{et}}$ along $c$. No bound on a tensor factor, invertibility of the projection map, or existence of points is assumed.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-constant-module-ordinary-realization to obtain the normalized ordinary scalar comparison and fixed inverse-image tensor data. The fixed inverse image is additive since it is a left adjoint between abelian categories, and the fixed direct image is additive since it is a right adjoint. The underlying fixed-module sheaf functor reflects finite limits. The geometric underlying comparison therefore makes the fixed inverse image left exact. Its adjunction supplies colimits. Reflect left exactness of the ringed inverse image along the exact scalar-restriction equivalence, using the ordinary left comparison; its adjunction supplies colimits. These constructions give ExactData without another assumption.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 07A6; canonical exact localization and adjunction transpose.

proof.text: Define the left derived comparison by the exact-functor composition isomorphisms and the localized ordinary left isomorphism. The composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations prove its complex and homotopy localization formulas. Its inverse has the inverse formula by cancellation. Define the right comparison to be its mate under the canonical exact/right-derived adjunctions. The vertical scalar functors are derived equivalences, so the standard iterated-mate argument makes that mate invertible. The derived exact-mate normalization lemma identifies its localization formula with the ordinary right comparison; the ordinary Hom equation identifies the latter with the ordinary mate. The unit-mate equation and naturality prove the derived Hom equation on every object. Applying this to identities and to counits proves the unit and counit squares.

proof.text: Apply the existing abstract projection-map mate compatibility theorem to the inverse left comparison. The tensor square is its comparison-compatibility hypothesis. The counit square identifies its mate with the chosen right comparison. Its conclusion is exactly ProjectionSquare. Package the comparisons, normalizations, tensor data, adjunction square and projection square into DerivedIdentification.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 07A6; canonical exact localization and adjunction transpose.

proof.text: Restrict the exact/right-derived unbounded adjunction along the two fully faithful bounded-below inclusions using the canonical plus compatibility isomorphisms. Its unit has the same homotopy localization equation as derivedPlus, so uniqueness of that unit identifies the two adjunctions. The restriction counit and Hom formulas give the included counit and Hom equations. Restrict the left comparison componentwise; conjugate the right comparison by the canonical plus direct-image compatibilities. Naturality follows from their three naturality squares. Faithfulness of the inclusion and cancellation of the fixed direct-image compatibility prove the bounded-below Hom square. This constructs PlusIdentification, including both included counit equations.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary etale geometric datum with its published fixed-module adjunction and canonical ordinary tensor data using lem-sfb-etale-constant-module-geometric-realization. Reuse the exactness, derived-identification and bounded-below constructors from the general comparison, retaining the canonical ordinary tensor data supplied by this realization, and choose the normalized scalar derived comparisons. This gives x,o,t,e and the bounded-below package. Use lem-sfb-etale-constant-module-tensor-normalization with the fixed tensor normalization field of e to identify its tensorator with the published K-flat etale tensorator under the canonical exact/left-derived isomorphism. The existing mapDerivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction_eq identifies the derived adjunctions under the same isomorphism; its Hom equation gives the full adjunction square, and identities and counits give the unit and counit squares. The abstract projection-map mate compatibility already proved in this module now supplies the projection square from the tensor and adjunction squares. Package these specified left and right isomorphisms, their reflexive normalization equations and the two squares into EtaleIdentification. No projection map is assumed invertible and no tensor bound or points are used.
